title: SRE, Platform & DevOps opportunities
lede: S.i. Systems' Networks and Infrastructure category, validated from full job descriptions. Scores measure technical and domain fit only.
latest_update: Rechecked September 21, 2026 — all 8 mandatory rendered-browser queries completed. Counts were 29, 41, 34, 31, 37, 24, 53 and 53; the first eight results of each reproduced the same previously validated candidate pool, with no new eligible posting.

notes_sections.heading: Run notes — full 8-query rotation
items: A first pass completed 2 of 8 queries (DevOps Engineer, Senior DevOps Engineer) before hitting a session budget limit; this run completed the remaining 6 (Site Reliability Engineer, Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer, DevSecOps Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, Senior Infrastructure Engineer) and merged results.

S.i. Systems' Networks and Infrastructure category is a small, static pool (~15-20 distinct live postings recurring across all query rankings, since q= is only a soft ranking signal per the skill). Confirmed this run: Site Reliability Engineer, Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, and Senior Infrastructure Engineer each surfaced only postings already scored from earlier queries within their first-8 boundary.

Cloud Engineer and DevSecOps Engineer each surfaced one new plausible candidate within the first-8 boundary: Network Analyst III (Toronto, WAN/LAN/Firewall/QoS troubleshooting) was screened out by title/summary alone — clearly network operations, not SRE/Platform/DevOps center of gravity, not opened. Senior Cloud Platform Engineer (8-10 years) (Job ID 154794) was opened, read in full, and scored -1/Ineligible below — real Azure/Terraform/Ansible/Databricks skill match, but Toronto Hybrid 4 days/week is outside the reachable-city range.

Infrastructure Engineer and Senior Infrastructure Engineer also surfaced two desktop-support/sysadmin-incident titles (Intermediate System Administrator — workstation/MS365 support; Systems Administrator — CyberArk incident support) screened out by title alone, not opened.
All retrieval was via a real browser, read-only; no application, account, or form action was used. No CAPTCHA encountered.

method: Eight independent searches were executed with expertise=3 in a rendered browser. Each query reached a real listing state and the first eight results were captured before deduplication. The soft keyword filter repeatedly returned the same small Networks and Infrastructure inventory. Current descriptions and applications.md statuses were reconciled; 12 previously validated rows remain, with no new eligible role and no inaccessible posting.
